title: For parents
lead: Does your child want to study in Italy? Naturally you have many questions: how much it costs, how the visa is obtained, who helps there. On this page we answer these questions openly and honestly.

a student can legally work per week

faq.q: How much does studying in Italy cost?
faq.a: At state universities the tuition fee is based on family income and is often low. For example, in Pisa in 2026/27 foreign students pay from 290 € to 2 900 € a year. A student who wins a scholarship (DSU) is fully exempt. Private universities are much more expensive, and living costs depend on the city.

faq.q: How do we show money for the visa?
faq.a: The embassy asks to see {{viza}} per year ({{vizaYil}}). This money is not spent: it is shown to be in your child's account or the family's (relatives up to the 4th degree). Prepare the money in advance and from a legal source: a large sum that suddenly appears in the last days raises questions.

Yes. By law, regional agencies give scholarships to students from low-income families, including foreigners. The minimum for {{dsuYil}} is {{stip}} per year. Conditions: family income and assets below the limits (ISEE {{isee}}, ISPE {{ispe}}) and the application submitted on time.

Family documents can only be obtained in Uzbekistan, so your help will be needed here.

Yes, up to 20 hours a week (1 040 hours a year) with an official contract. But in the first year it is better to focus on studies: to keep the scholarship, exams must be passed. Set aside money for the first 3–4 months, because the scholarship usually arrives late.

faq.q: Who helps there? What about health?
faq.a:
Within 8 days of arrival, an application for the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) is made. For health the student registers with the national system (SSN) for {{ssn}} a year or takes private insurance; in an emergency 112 works. The university has an international students office, and many cities have an Uzbek student community.

The first year is not easy: bureaucracy is slow, the language unfamiliar, homesickness natural. If you know this in advance, you can prepare your child emotionally too.

faq.q: Is the degree recognised? And after studies?
faq.a: An Italian degree is recognised in Europe. After graduating, if the conditions are met, the student permesso can be converted into a job-seeking permesso for up to 12 months. With an Italian permesso you can travel to other Schengen countries for up to 90 days within 180 days.

faq.q: How do we work with Uniroad? Do you give guarantees?
faq.a:
No one can honestly guarantee admission or a visa: the university and the embassy decide. We help you complete every step correctly and on time.

The information and tools on the site are free. As a parent you can ask any question yourself on Telegram.

warnings: If someone says «I will get you the visa 100%», be careful: nobody can guarantee that.
Pay university, CIMEA and embassy fees only through their official website or cashier.
Do not leave original documents (passport, diploma) with strangers. If someone else submits for the DoV, they do so with an official power of attorney.
Do not transfer money for housing in Italy without seeing it and signing a contract.
Check every date and amount against the official source. Do not rely on «a friend told me» posts on social media.
docs: For the scholarship: family composition, each member's income and housing documents, with apostille and Italian translation. The exact list by region is on the «Scholarship» page.
As a visa sponsor: bank statement, certificate of employment and salary, letter of no objection. The full list is in step 5.
